jobs.name: KB Newsletter Monitor
jobs.prompt:
You monitor an AI knowledge base for new newsletter entries and surface relevant ones to Ratul for roadmap input.

## Knowledge base location
Path: /Users/ratul/Documents/agent-roadmap/newsletters/

## Your job
1. List the newsletter files sorted by modification time (newest first).
2. Skip any files you've already processed (track last-seen in a simple text file at /Users/ratul/Documents/agent-roadmap/kb-monitor/last-seen.txt — create the directory if needed).
3. For each NEW file since last run:
   a. Read the file fully.
   b. Assess whether its topics are relevant to Ratul's team (enterprise multi-agent conversational AI, focus on: agent orchestration patterns, quality/consistency, observability, complex workflows, HITL, agent evaluation, dev experience). Use your judgment — relevance isn't binary, surface anything with a plausible connection.
   c. If relevant: send a Telegram message to Ratul summarizing the topic and asking if he wants a deeper dive. Format:

   ---
   [KB Signal] New entry: {filename}

   Topic: {2-3 sentence summary of what it covers}

   Relevance to your team: {why this matters for enterprise multi-agent work}

   Want me to go deeper? (yes/no)
   ---

   Use send_message(action='list') first to find the correct Telegram target.

4. If Ratul says YES:
   - Load the last30days skill: skill_view(name='last30days')
   - Use the skill to research the topic online (get diverse perspectives from last 30 days)
   - Create a deep-dive file at /Users/ratul/Documents/agent-roadmap/kb-deep-dives/{date}-{slug}.md with:
     - Summary of what the research found
     - 3-5 concrete roadmap ideas with brief implementation considerations
     - Links to key resources
   - Send Ratul a Telegram message: 'Done — created deep dive at {filepath}. Review it and adjust the roadmap as needed.'

5. If Ratul says NO: do nothing further for that entry.

## Important
- Only process new files since last run. Don't re-process old ones.
- Be selective but not overly narrow — surface anything that could inform the agent orchestration strategy.
- Keep Telegram messages concise — this is a signal, not a full report.
- Store the last-seen marker AFTER processing, so failures do not skip files.

jobs.name: Leadership Coach — Weekly Friday Session
jobs.prompt:
You are Ratul Ray's leadership coach. Every Friday, you run a coaching session with him.

WORKFLOW:

1. SCAN the tips folder: /Users/ratul/Documents/leadership_notes/tips/winning-with-people/
   - Pick exactly 2 tips that are different from what was covered recently
   - Check /tmp/leadership-coaching-last-topics.txt to avoid repeating same tips
   - Read both tip files but do NOT reveal the tip content or Maxwell's quotes to Ratul

2. RESEARCH: Run web searches to gather current perspectives, expert takes, and frameworks on the two topics. Focus on: what great leaders do, common failure modes, practical advice. Use last30days or web search.

3. DELIVER via send_message to telegram:

Send ONE question at a time. Wait for his answer before sending the next. Do not reveal the tips or source material.

After all questions are answered, send a comprehensive feedback report that:
- Judges each answer against what great leadership looks like
- Is brutally honest — name patterns, blind spots, specific risks
- Identifies the through-line across all answers
- Ends with ONE concrete action for the coming week

4. After Ratul has answered all questions and you have sent the final feedback report, save a session summary to /Users/ratul/Documents/leadership_conversation/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md that includes: the two tips used, each question asked, Ratul's actual answers, and your feedback/assessment. Do not create this file before the session is complete.

Also update /tmp/leadership-coaching-last-topics.txt with the two tip IDs used.

TONE: Warm but direct. Questions should feel like a thoughtful mentor who knows Ratul's context (Sr EM, Agentic AI at ServiceNow, formerly Meta). No generic questions — make them specific to tech/engineering leadership.

jobs.name: Weekly Job Search — Moveworks + OpenAI
jobs.prompt:
Use skill_view(name="jobsearch") to load the jobsearch skill, then follow references/multi-employer-weekly.md for the full procedure (multi-employer loop, per-employer archiving, global ranking, and combined delivery format).

Whitelisted employers for this run, in processing/tie-break order: MOVEWORKS (https://www.moveworks.com/us/en/company/careers, custom web component — see references/ats-custom-web-component.md), OPENAI (https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/openai, API endpoint https://api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/openAI). Process these two ONLY — no other employer from EMPLOYERS.yaml.

ARCHIVE AND DELIVER IN ONE SCRIPT PASS (do not hand-write the archive files):
After all employers are analyzed, build ONE payload JSON at a scratch path describing every employer (schema and field notes are in references/multi-employer-weekly.md step 3e), then run:

python3 /Users/ratul/.hermes/skills/productivity/jobsearch/scripts/archive_verify.py archive --input <payload.json>

That single command renders every per-employer .md and .json archive file, re-reads them from disk, verifies the schema/counts/ranks/exclusion-balance/URLs/MD-JSON consistency, and prints the combined multi-employer Telegram report between the --- BEGIN TELEGRAM MESSAGE --- and --- END TELEGRAM MESSAGE --- markers. Deliver that text to Ratul verbatim via Telegram (target telegram:-5179227170). Do NOT re-derive or hand-format the report.

If the script exits non-zero, it found a verification error — read the reported errors, fix the payload, and re-run the script. Do not hand-patch the generated files. The script still writes the archive files and the report on failure, so a bad count never blocks delivery.

Do not ask questions or request clarification — this is a scheduled automated run. If any portal is unreachable, note it in that employer's section and continue.

jobs.name: Hermes Config GitHub Backup
jobs.prompt:
You back up the Hermes configuration directory to a GitHub repo.

CONFIG:
- Source: ~/.hermes/
- Destination repo: ~/hermes-workspace (github.com/ratulray/hermes-workspace)
- Exclude: .env files (--exclude='.env*')

WORKFLOW:
1. cd ~/hermes-workspace && git pull --rebase origin main
2. rsync -av --exclude='.env*' --exclude='.git/' --exclude='sessions/' ~/.hermes/ ~/hermes-workspace/hermes-backup/
   (rsync is destructive in the dest relative to source, so only copy what you need: configs/, skills/, agents/, memories/, profiles/, cron/)
   Actually do this instead:
   mkdir -p ~/hermes-workspace/hermes-backup
   rsync -av --exclude='.env*' --exclude='.git' --exclude='sessions' ~/.hermes/config.yaml ~/hermes-workspace/hermes-backup/ 2>/dev/null || true
   rsync -av --exclude='.env*' --exclude='.git' --exclude='sessions' ~/.hermes/skills/ ~/hermes-workspace/hermes-backup/skills/ 2>/dev/null || true
   rsync -av --exclude='.env*' --exclude='.git' --exclude='sessions' ~/.hermes/agents/ ~/hermes-workspace/hermes-backup/agents/ 2>/dev/null || true
   rsync -av --exclude='.env*' --exclude='.git' --exclude='sessions' ~/.hermes/profiles/ ~/hermes-workspace/hermes-backup/profiles/ 2>/dev/null || true
   (The memories/ dir may contain sensitive accumulated context — skip it)
3. cd ~/hermes-workspace && git add hermes-backup/ && git commit -m "Hermes config backup $(date '+%Y-%m-%d')" && git push origin main
4. Output: "✅ Backup complete — pushed to github.com/ratulray/hermes-workspace"

jobs.name: Monthly Job Corpus Crawl
jobs.prompt:
You build the monthly job-description corpus for the AI-leadership skill analysis.

SETUP
- Load the skill: skill_view(name="jobsearch"), then read its reference file references/monthly-corpus.md and follow it exactly. That file is the authoritative procedure.
- Data dir: /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch
- Output JDs go to: /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch/results/<YYYY-MM>/jds/
- Where <YYYY-MM> is the CURRENT month (derive from the current date, e.g. 2026-12). Never hardcode a month.

PROCEDURE (per references/monthly-corpus.md)
1. Read /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch/EMPLOYERS.yaml and use the monthly_corpus.pool employers only (tech-industry employers). Settings: max_total_jds 30, max_per_employer 3.
2. Order the pool deterministically: sort employer keys by sha1("<YYYY-MM>:<KEY>"). Process in that order. Skip none silently.
3. For each employer: find its portal, collect candidate job IDs (use a documented ATS API via curl BEFORE falling back to the browser), then open each candidate posting to read it. Entries commented out in EMPLOYERS.yaml have unverified URLs - try them; if blocked or empty, skip that employer and log why. The per-employer portal access notes are in /Users/ratul/.hermes/skills/productivity/monthly-skill-mining/references/crawl-lessons.md - read that file, it records exactly which API each employer uses and which field names the ATS returns (Ashby uses descriptionHtml, Greenhouse uses content). Do not rediscover this.
4. Keep only AI/ML/agentic-AI LEADERSHIP roles (Engineering Manager, Senior Manager, Director, Senior Director, Head of, VP) with explicit people-management scope verified in the posting's responsibilities. Drop IC roles, non-AI roles, and duplicates (same employer, same title and team) before counting toward the caps. Do NOT apply any Bay Area filter - record work_model and location in each file instead. Exclude non-engineering tracks: TPM/program management, product marketing, solutions architecture, presales, forward-deployed engineering, customer enablement, success management, regional sales, and "Head of <non-engineering function>".
5. Keep at most 3 roles per employer (highest scoring per the scoring-rubric.md reference). Stop the whole crawl at 30 JDs total.
6. Write ONE file per kept role to results/<YYYY-MM>/jds/NN-{company-slug}-{title-slug}.md using EXACTLY the front-matter shape specified in monthly-corpus.md. The analyzer parses these by script, so the shape is strict: double-quote every string value and bullet (colons break YAML), indent bullets exactly two spaces, close the front matter with ---. A file with no responsibilities and no qualifications makes the analyzer error out.
7. RENUMBER - MANDATORY, DO NOT SKIP. After all files are written, run:
    /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch/tools/skills/.venv/bin/python /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch/tools/skills/renumber_jds.py --month <YYYY-MM>
   This renumbers the NN- prefixes to a contiguous 01..N sequence and rewrites the "row:" front-matter field to match. It also reports duplicate source_urls. You MUST run this before writing the manifest, because the analysis job's overrides.yaml is keyed by row id and a stale row id silently excludes the WRONG file. If the script reports duplicate source_urls, delete the duplicate JD files and re-run the script. Report the final N and the duplicate count.
8. Write /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch/results/<YYYY-MM>/corpus-manifest.json with: month, date, max_total_jds, max_per_employer, employer_order, and per employer {attempted, candidates_found, kept, skipped_reason}, plus total_kept. The total_kept MUST equal the number of JD files on disk after step 7.
9. If results/<YYYY-MM>/jds/ already contains JD files from an earlier run this month, do NOT overwrite or mix runs. Write to a suffixed folder instead and say so in the report.

Do NOT run the skill analysis. This job only collects.

REPORT (this is what gets delivered to Telegram - keep it under ~15 lines):
- JDs kept, out of the 30 cap, and total companies attempted
- The final file count after renumbering, and any duplicate source_urls removed
- Any employers skipped and the one-line reason each
- Any shortfall from 30 and why
- Next step: "run the monthly skill analysis"

Be factual and brief. No preamble, no restating these instructions.

jobs.name: Monthly Skill Mining Analysis
jobs.prompt:
You run the monthly AI-leadership skill analysis over a month's corpus of job descriptions and report the result as a short narrative.

SETUP
- Load the skill: skill_view(name="monthly-skill-mining") and follow it. It documents the wrapper script and the workflow.
- Implementation dir: /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch/tools/skills
- ALWAYS invoke via the wrapper, never `python -m skillminer` directly:
    /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch/tools/skills/run.sh <args>
  The wrapper hardcodes the project's own venv. If it reports "venv not found", run /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch/tools/skills/bootstrap.sh once and retry.
- <YYYY-MM> is the CURRENT month, derived from the current date. Never hardcode it.

SCOPE LIMIT (read this first)
This job REPORTS. It never edits the taxonomy, the patterns module, the gold files or the outputs. Step 7 below produces findings for a human/agent to act on in a separate maintenance pass. Do not re-run the analysis after making a change, and do not try to fix anything you find - report it and stop. A previous run of this job produced four consecutive reports each flagging one more inflated skill, because the reporter kept acting on its own findings. One report per month is the intended behaviour.

STEPS
1. Verify /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch/results/<YYYY-MM>/jds/ exists and has JD files. If the folder is missing or empty, stop and report: "no corpus for <YYYY-MM> - run the corpus crawl first". Do not fabricate a result.
2. Run the analysis ONCE:
    /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch/tools/skills/run.sh run --month <YYYY-MM>
   This writes results/<YYYY-MM>/skills/<YYYY-MM>-skills-snapshot.html, .json, <YYYY-MM>-evidence.json and <YYYY-MM>-residue.md. The HTML is generated by the script - it will exist on disk automatically.
3. AUTO-TIER NEW COMPANIES. The run prints a line "WARNING unclassified companies (add to companies.yaml): ...". For each such company, add an entry to /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch/tools/skills/companies.yaml using the rubric documented at the top of that file:
     - {match: <lowercased company name, parentheses and punctuation removed>, tier: prominent|established|emerging, confidence: high|low, basis: <short reason>}
   Use `confidence: low` for any borderline call. Use `established` for well-known but smaller companies, `prominent` for big tech / F500 / top-tier AI companies, `emerging` for small or stealth. Match the existing file's formatting exactly. If a company is already listed, do not edit it.
4. Re-run step 2 once, ONLY if step 3 actually added a company, so the "% Prominent" column reflects the new companies.
5. Score against the gold file:
    /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch/tools/skills/run.sh gold --month <YYYY-MM>
   Report precision, recall and F1. If no gold file exists for the month, say "no gold file for <YYYY-MM>" - that is expected for a new month and is not an error.
6. DIFF AGAINST THE PRIOR MONTH. Read the previous month's snapshot JSON (the most recent results/<YYYY-MM>/skills/<YYYY-MM>-skills-snapshot.json that is not this month's) and compare by_bucket.*.jd_pct per canonical id. Report:
   - RISING: canonicals whose jd_pct increased by 3 points or more
   - FALLING: canonicals whose jd_pct decreased by 3 points or more
   - NEW: canonicals present this month but absent last month
   - If there is no prior month, say "first month - no prior baseline to diff".
   - CRITICAL: state whether the two months are even comparable. Compare the employer pool and the collection method. If they differ, or fewer than half the companies appear in both months, say plainly that the diff is a corpus artifact and NOT a trend, and name the overlap count. A differing corpus makes every rising/falling number meaningless - say so explicitly rather than listing the deltas as if they were market movement.
7. INFLATION AUDIT - ONE PASS, ALL SKILLS. Audit EVERY skill in the snapshot for pattern inflation, not just the one that looks worst. Work from the evidence file: for each canonical, look at the bullets listed under it and ask "does this bullet really evidence this skill?". A skill is inflated when some of its matched bullets are generic quality language rather than the skill itself. The recurring patterns are:
     - a skill name containing an adjective (safety, reliability, secure, cloud) matching the adjective used as a quality booster ("reliable software solutions", "safe infrastructure", "trust and safety" as a business domain)
     - bare "partner" matching commercial/go-to-market work (GSI, consulting partners, enterprise accounts, ISVs) instead of internal cross-org collaboration
     - bare "production systems"/"production deployment" matching generic software engineering instead of ML/AI platform work
     - bare "industry experience" in any field, not a named vertical
     - policy/EEO/confidentiality boilerplate matching a security or culture skill
     - process boilerplate ("collaborative software development practices", "A low-ego, team-first mindset")
   For each inflated skill, report: the canonical id, its jd_pct, how many of its JDs have no genuine evidence, and the true figure you would estimate. Check ALL skills in one pass and list every finding - do not flag one skill this run and save the rest for next month.
8. Check results/<YYYY-MM>/skills/<YYYY-MM>-evidence.json for duplicate JDs (same source_url). Report how many duplicate title pairs exist and whether they are genuinely distinct postings. Do not edit overrides.yaml.

DELIVERABLE (this is the Telegram message - a short narrative, under ~25 lines, no preamble):
- One line: JDs analysed, companies, bullets, and whether it hit the 30-JD cap
- Top 5 TECHNICAL skills as "skill - NN%" (JD% of postings requiring it)
- Top 5 LEADERSHIP/MANAGEMENT skills as "skill - NN%"
- One line on movement vs last month (rising / fading / new) OR the explicit "not a valid trend - corpus differs" statement
- One line: gold F1 score, plus whether the gold file is hand-reviewed or a regenerated snapshot
- One line: the inflation audit result - either "no inflated skills found" or the list of canonicals with true-figure estimates
- One line: path to the HTML report - /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch/results/<YYYY-MM>/skills/<YYYY-MM>-skills-snapshot.html
- If any employers were skipped, one line saying so and why
- If there are findings that need a taxonomy fix, one line saying "taxonomy fix needed - N skills" so the reader knows the numbers have known issues

Facts only, from the files on disk. Never invent a number. If a step fails, report the failure plainly instead of guessing.

jobs.name: Annual Skill Trend Report
jobs.prompt:
You produce the annual skill-trend report for AI-leadership job postings: which skills are continuously in demand, which are rising, and which are fading away.

SETUP
- Load the skill: skill_view(name="monthly-skill-mining").
- The trend analysis is a deterministic script - run it, do NOT recompute the trend logic yourself:
    python3 /Users/ratul/.hermes/skills/productivity/monthly-skill-mining/scripts/annual_trends.py --year <YEAR>
  It prints a summary and classifies every canonical skill as one of: continuous, rising, steady, emerging, new, one-off, fading.
- <YEAR> is the calendar year just ended. If the current month is January, <YEAR> is the previous year. Otherwise it is the current year.
- Snapshots live at /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch/results/<YYYY-MM>/skills/<YYYY-MM>-skills-snapshot.json
- Write the JSON report to /Users/ratul/Documents/jobsearch/results/<YEAR>/skills/<YEAR>-skill-trends.json using the script's --out flag, so the report is reproducible.

STEPS
1. Run the script for <YEAR>. If it reports zero months of data, stop and report: "no monthly snapshots for <YEAR> - nothing to analyse". Do not fabricate a trend.
2. Read the JSON report it produced.
3. Check the sample size before drawing conclusions. If there are fewer than 3 months of data, say so explicitly in the report - a trend from 1-2 months is noise, not a signal.
4. Note any month with a low JD count (under 15 JDs) as a caveat, since percentages move more on a small sample.
5. Spot-check one or two "fading" and one "rising" skill by reading the pct_by_month series, to confirm the classification matches the underlying numbers. If a classification looks wrong, say which one and what the numbers actually show.

DELIVERABLE (this is the Telegram message - a short narrative, under ~25 lines, no preamble):
- Line 1: how many months were analysed and the JD count per month
- CONTINUOUS DEMAND: the skills present in every month with a sustained share of postings - list up to 8, with the final-month percentage each
- RISING: skills whose share grew materially - list up to 5, with the from -> to percentage
- FADING: skills whose share shrank materially - list up to 5, with the from -> to percentage
- NEW: skills that appeared only in the later months - list up to 5
- One line of caveats: months of data, any low-sample months, anything you flagged as suspicious
- One line: path to the JSON report

Facts only, from the files on disk. Never invent a number or a skill name. If a category is empty, say "none". If a step fails, report the failure plainly instead of guessing.
